project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 276 (System rejects a revision count above 10 while the pool holds between 20 and 50 worlds, so the selection bar stays low)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 276 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the middle rung of docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §12.1's pool-size ladder — the ceiling that keeps a thin pool's sweep narrow so the selection bar stays low. One new module, dreaming/ceiling.py, holding one free function, rejects_uncapped_sweep(revision_count, world_count, *, floor=20, full_dreaming=50, ceiling=10), a verdict over counts the caller already has (the same shape feature 275's rejects_thin_pool takes): raises RevisionCeilingError when the revision count exceeds the band's ceiling while the pool sits in the 20–50 band, returns without raising above it (the pool has cleared 50, feature 277's raise has fired, and M is that feature's to answer at 40), and delegates a pool below the floor to feature 275's own rejects_thin_pool so the bottom rung is refused in the floor's own word (pool_too_thin) by the floor's own one spelling of the rule — which is what depends_on 275 means in code. The band's three figures are CONSUMED, never respelled: the ceiling defaults to feature 277's CAPPED_SWEEP_CAP (10 — the same constant that feature's schedule answers on this band, imported from dreaming.cap), the band's lower edge to feature 275's LADDER_FLOOR_WORLDS (20), and its upper edge to feature 277's FULL_DREAMING_WORLDS (50). This is what makes the entitlement and the refusal one number: the default judgment admits exactly what dreaming.cap.revision_cap answers, at every pool size, by construction rather than by agreement. One new error sibling under DreamingError — RevisionCeilingError, deliberately WITHOUT a code word (feature 276's sentence mandates none; feature 275's pool_too_thin is mandated by its own), whose repair (lower M to the band's cap, or grow the pool until the raise applies) is neither the floor's (grow the pool before dreaming at all) nor feature 277's CapRequestError's (re-consider the ask) — so a caller can catch each apart. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no new @register component and no seat edit (feature 270's single "dreaming" component is untouched); no table, no persistence, no third party — the module imports typing, the member's own .cap, .errors and .ladder, and nothing else, so the factory's scan pays nothing for the ceiling.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`, and the seats in src/app/modules/ <member>/ are reached as submodules. A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and `packages/dreaming/tests/`). The repository venv is created by a bare `uv sync`, which does NOT install pyarrow/polars; the repo-level suite therefore fails collection in tests/contract and tests/feature-store with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'polars'` until `uv sync --all-packages` is run. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. The dreaming member is stdlib-only, and feature 276 keeps it that way: `typing` plus the member's own modules, and no more.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md sections, stdlib-only computation, a verdict-gate free function (raises on refusal, returns otherwise) rather than an evaluator or a component, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition, and the error-vocabulary discipline: one base class per member, the subclasses split by the repair a caller must make (not by which line raised), no member imports another, and a caller must be able to catch one feature's refusal without catching a neighbouring feature's — so a shared rule is translated at the seam rather than re-raised in a neighbour's class. Features 270 (the cycle freeze, cycle.py), 275 (the ladder floor, ladder.py) and 277 (the revision cap's schedule and record, cap.py) already live in this member; feature 276 is a fourth sentence within it, not a new member — and it is the middle rung the other two bracket, so it consumes their figures rather than restating them.

category.name: Dreaming Loop & Meta-Selection
category.feature: System rejects a revision count above 10 while the pool holds between 20 and 50 worlds, so the selection bar stays low.

project_specification.integration_points: The judgment is a free function in the dreaming member's new ceiling module, reached directly from the member (`from dreaming import rejects_uncapped_sweep, RevisionCeilingError`) and re-exported by the member __init__, the way feature 275's floor names are. No composed application needs a second component: feature 270's single "dreaming" component (the CycleFreeze) is untouched, and the seat (src/app/modules/dreaming) is not edited — the floor set that precedent and feature 276 follows it, exactly as feature 277 did. The two counts the judgment reads are ones the caller already has at the point §C5's loop needs them: the pool's size is recorded by the hold the cycle opened (a feature-270 FreezeRecord carries world_count, and pool_commitment computes it), and the revision count is the caller's own intent for the sweep it is about to run. Feature 277's schedule (dreaming.cap.revision_cap) answers the cap a cycle is *entitled to* on each rung and this judgment refuses the count it is *allowed* — they are the same 10 on the band, consumed from the one constant, so the loop calls revision_cap for M and rejects_uncapped_sweep to enforce the ceiling, and the two can never disagree. Neither judgment opens a database.
project_specification.constraints: - The ceiling applies to exactly ONE rung and is exact at both edges: world_count >= 50 admits any revision count (feature 277's raise has fired; the top rung has no ceiling); 20 <= world_count < 50 admits a count <= ceiling and refuses a count > ceiling; world_count < 20 is refused by feature 275's own rejects_thin_pool in its own word (pool_too_thin). - The band's three figures are consumed, never respelled: ceiling defaults to dreaming.cap.CAPPED_SWEEP_CAP (10), full_dreaming to dreaming.cap.FULL_DREAMING_WORLDS (50), floor to dreaming.ladder. LADDER_FLOOR_WORLDS (20). No ladder figure is spelled as a literal in the new module. The default judgment must never refuse what revision_cap(world_count) answers, at any pool size. - One new error sibling under DreamingError — RevisionCeilingError — that borrows none of the member's existing five classes and is borrowed by none of them. It carries no code word: feature 276's sentence mandates none, and every message opens with its subject (the count, the ceiling, the band and the pool's size), states the repair (lower M to the band's cap, or grow the pool until the raise applies), names §12.1 and cites Appendix B's sqrt(2 ln M) bar and the section's n > 53 at M = 40. The one thin-pool refusal this feature mints is feature 275's, delegated, in feature 275's word. - The judgment is a verdict over counts, not a count the feature performs: rejects_uncapped_sweep takes both figures as arguments and opens no database, reads no pool row, resolves no path and imports nothing that could (no sqlite3, no sqlite_path, no connection). A malformed count or rung is refused rather than answered, so a cycle whose inputs are wrong is never silently admitted or blocked on a value that is not a count. - The floor keyword passes straight through to the ladder's gate, and a malformed floor is refused by ladder.validated_floor in the ladder's own class (PoolTooThinError), because the floor is feature 275's fact. A boundary below the floor is refused in this feature's class, naming both edges. - No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited. No new @register component, no table, no persistence, and no seat export: feature 270's single "dreaming" component is the member's whole composition and its suite (test_component.py) is untouched. - All existing tests in the dreaming member (packages/dreaming/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare `uv run pytest` gate). - Do not edit the order-sensitive shared files: src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/**.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the class and the judgment. Add RevisionCeilingError(DreamingError) to dreaming.errors as a sibling of the member's existing five classes, following the repair-split discipline (the repair for a too-wide sweep is neither to grow the pool before dreaming at all — the floor's — nor to re-send a malformed ask — the cap's — but to lower M to the band's cap or grow the pool until the raise applies), and extend the errors module docstring with the ladder's third rung. Add dreaming/ceiling.py with the three input validators (the revision count, the pool figure and the band's upper edge, each in this module's own vocabulary; the floor delegated to ladder.validated_floor) and rejects_uncapped_sweep(revision_count, world_count, *, floor=20, full_dreaming=50, ceiling=10) — a pure function that validates in the documented order, refuses a boundary below the floor, delegates the thin judgment to rejects_thin_pool, returns without raising at or above the upper edge, and raises RevisionCeilingError above the ceiling inside the band. Re-export the function and the class from the member __init__.py.

Phase 2 — the tests. Add packages/dreaming/tests/test_ceiling.py pinning: the exact band (20 and 49 refuse a count of 11; 20 and 49 admit 10), both edges (the inclusive admitted side, the floor as the band's first pool, 49 capped against 50 raised), the absence of a ceiling above the band (40 and 1000 admitted at 50, 60, 500), the consumed-constant law (the module attributes ARE dreaming.cap's objects; the default judgment admits revision_cap(world_count) for every pool from 20 to 200 and refuses exactly revision_cap + 1 below the band only), zero revisions admitted on every rung, the refusal's content (both figures, both edges, §12.1, the sqrt(2 ln M) bar, n > 53, and the two half-repairs), the parameters and their validation (a custom ceiling, a zero ceiling, a custom upper edge, a raised floor, the boundary-below-floor refusal, and the degenerate floor-equals-edge case), the pure-function shape verified by denial (no sqlite3 / sqlite_path / connect on the module), every malformed input in the right class (a bool/float/str/negative count or figure refused in this module's class, a malformed floor in the ladder's), the delegated thin refusal (pool_too_thin, §12.1 named, winning over the ceiling when both facts are true, and the delegation pinned as the floor's own function object), and the vocabulary siblinghood (five ways, no code word, and the module spelling no ladder literal). Extend test_errors.py with the ceiling class's sibling test. Run both suites and lint only the changed files against a sibling.
